Process: Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) grown in a fed-batch bioreactor. Biomass concentration x1 and substrate (glucose) concentration x2 are measured every hour, in g/L. The operator sets the dilution rate u1 (1/h) and the substrate concentration in the feed u2 (g/L), both held constant between switches. Three experiments of 20 h with different starting biomass and input profiles. Measurement error is about 5% of the reading plus 0.01 g/L. The growth kinetics are unknown: find the rate law that explains the data.

Fitted candidates (all on the same data, 126 readings):

Round 1 of 3. Decide. If you accept, 'chosen' is the candidate label, e.g. C8.

answer.feedback: No candidate qualifies. Refine the kinetics or model structure to address the near-best Monod model’s systematic residuals: it under-predicts x2 in E2 (especially early, worst at 1 h) and E3 (worst at 11 h), and over-predicts x1 in E1 (worst at 9 h). The Andrews candidate still under-predicts E2 x2, but reverses the E3 x2 error to over-prediction; its inhibition parameter Ki is not estimated precisely, so these results do not establish substrate inhibition. The supplied summaries do not identify whether these times are at high or low substrate—use the experiment profiles to check that when designing the next search.
answer.reasoning: C8 has severe lack of fit. C9 has the highest Akaike weight but still exceeds its 95% chi-square limit, so it cannot be accepted. C40 also exceeds its limit and additionally has an imprecise Ki estimate (t=0.57). Thus none fits within the noise with every parameter estimated precisely.
